cohort: 1,000 newborns up to 28 days of life, all with maternal risk factors, born in a tertiary care center and admitted to the NICU.
finding: Several maternal risk factors, including previous bad obstetric histories, pregnancy-induced hypertension, and previous lower segment cesarean section, were associated with higher NICU admissions and neonatal morbidities and mortality, with respiratory distress syndrome being the leading cause of morbidity.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were more commonly associated with NICU admissions.
gest_age: The majority of NICU admissions occurred during 34-36 weeks of gestation.
